title: Putting a guessed feeling into words for a baby
summary: CDC suggests using words, face, and voice to show what you think a 9-month-old is feeling, for example by saying the baby is sad and offering comfort.
body: The CDC 9-month activity notes say to use words, facial expressions, and voice to show what you think the baby is feeling, and the feelings it names are sad, mad, and happy. The example sentence on the page is telling the baby they are sad and seeing whether they can be helped to feel better. The tip is a suggestion for talking with a baby. It does not say the caregiver's guess is always right, and it is not a mood report about a stranger.

sources.title: Milestones by 9 Months
sources.author: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.note: US government public domain. Supports the tip to name a guessed feeling such as sad, mad, or happy and to offer comfort.
